title: Over Forty Percent of Patients In Medical Cannabis Pain Study Stay In Program For A Year, Says Report
description: First, a confession. The actual title of the report was “Majority of Chronic Pain Patients Discontinue Medical Cannabis Within One Year, New Study ...
content_html_sanitized:
First, a confession. The actual title of the report was “Majority of Chronic Pain Patients Discontinue Medical Cannabis Within One Year, New Study Finds.

 

Of course, both are mathematically correct, but is the glass 56% empty or 44% full?

 

Actually, “nearly half—44.7 percent—quit in the first three months.” And these were the oldest patients in the study, and “those who discontinued were, on average, about seven years older than those who continued, with mean ages of 71.5 years and 64.5 years, respectively.”

See AMA Reports More Seniors Using Marijuana. Maybe It’s Because Common Drugs That They Prescribe Are Tied to Increased Risk of Cognitive Decline In Seniors But Marijuana Helps.

 

It seems likely that the older group had problems with cannabis psychoactive effects, not with the lack of pain relief.

Consider these other recent findings.

See Opening Legal Marijuana Dispensaries Is Tied To A Huge Drop In Opioid-Related Deaths, Analysis Finds

And

Analysis: Medical Cannabis Associated With Reduced Healthcare Utilization in Chronic Pain Patients

And

Recreational, Sacramental and Medical: Why There’s No Clear Delineation Between Recreational and Medical Cannabis.

And

For a more comprehensive statistical analysis see

Nearly 4 In 10 Californians Are Current Marijuana Users—And Most Report Health Benefits, Study Shows

And

8 In 10 Marijuana Consumers Use It As A Substitute For Prescription Drugs, New Survey Finds

And

The holistic effects of medical cannabis compared to opioids on pain experience in Finnish patients with chronic pain

It’s complicated, but it is also absurd that almost 30 years after Proposition 215, the first medical marijuana initiative, was passed in California, we are still at this basic level.

 

From October 24, 2000

See Transcript of 1996 Conversation Between the Czar and the Former Managing Editor of New York Times About Medical Marijuana Initiatives Gives Great Insight Into How Marijuana Prohibition Really Works.

(I would recommend that you have a strong anti nausea medication handy when you read this.)
